name: Choroid Plexus Tumor

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Histopathological confirmation of tumor arising from choroid plexus epithelium
MRI or CT showing intraventricular mass with characteristic enhancement and location
Signs of increased intracranial pressure such as headache, vomiting, and papilledema

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation plus compatible imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular markers may assist in distinguishing papilloma from carcinoma.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to cerebrospinal fluid overproduction or obstruction
searchTerms: brain fluid buildup from blockage or overproduction
hydrocephalus caused by CSF flow problems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intraventricular mass lesion detected on neuroimaging
searchTerms: brain imaging shows mass in ventricles

common.symptomName: Headache secondary to increased intracranial pressure
searchTerms: head pain due to increased intracranial pressure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure
optic disc swelling seen on eye exam
epileptic episodes due to brain lesion

occasional.symptomName: Ataxia or gait disturbance from cerebellar compression
searchTerms: balance and walking problems from cerebellar pressure
difficulty coordinating movements from cerebellar involvement

occasional.symptomName: Visual field defects due to optic pathway involvement
searchTerms: blind spots from optic nerve damage
visual field loss due to nerve involvement
weakness on one side of body
endocrine issues caused by brain lesion
respiratory irregularities from brain fluid buildup
abnormal breathing linked to increased brain pressure

rare.symptomName: Subarachnoid hemorrhage due to tumor vascularity
searchTerms: bleeding around brain from tumor blood vessels
sudden brain bleed due to tumor vascularity

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal but may show elevated protein
imaging: MRI shows well-circumscribed intraventricular mass with intense contrast enhancement
CT may reveal calcifications within tumor
genetic: Alterations in TP53 gene in choroid plexus carcinoma
Chromosomal abnormalities such as gains in chromosome 7
other: Histopathology reveals papillary architecture with fibrovascular cores
Immunohistochemistry positive for cytokeratin and transthyretin

distinguishingFeatures: Ependymomas arise from ependymal lining, often located in posterior fossa or spinal cord
Different histopathological features lacking papillary structures
Medulloblastomas are midline cerebellar tumors common in children
More aggressive with distinct molecular subtypes

redFlags: Rapidly increasing head circumference in infants
Signs of acute hydrocephalus such as sudden vomiting or decreased consciousness
references: Louis DN et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition, 2021
